worldsinglass.handbook.page.1:
§lThe Globe Keeper's Handbook§r


Notes on worlds kept under glass, by Odile, glassblower of the northern pass.

§o(Read on, and look after them.)
worldsinglass.handbook.page.2:
My grandmother said every snow globe holds a real winter, very far away and very small.

She was half right. They aren't far away at all.

Hold one close, crouch low, and press your eye to the glass...
worldsinglass.handbook.page.3:
...and you'll be standing inside.

The glass becomes your sky. The room you left becomes a land of giants: your own house, a hundred times over, with whoever's at home peering in at you.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.4:
§lThe pipe§r

Every globe starts as a breath of glass. Make a §8glassblower's pipe§r: two iron ingots and a copper ingot, corner to corner.

The pipe and three glass blocks blow a §8glass bulb§r. The pipe comes back, a little worn.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.5:
§lMaking globes§r

A bulb, over what goes inside, over a base:

§8Snow globe§r: a snow block, on a wooden slab
§8Terrarium§r: moss, on three slabs
§8Storm globe§r: a lightning rod, on copper
§8Desert globe§r: a dead bush, on cut sandstone
worldsinglass.handbook.page.6:
§8Aquarium§r: kelp, on three dark prismarine slabs
§8Star globe§r: a spyglass, on amethyst
§8Nether jar§r: a blackstone slab lid, the bulb, a magma block
§8Ship in a bottle§r: a bulb, a boat and a stripped oak log, any way round
worldsinglass.handbook.page.7:
§lHandling§r

§8Right-click§r the glass to shake it.
§8Sneak + right-click§r to step inside.
§8Right-click the base§r to turn it.
§8Punch§r the glass to knock: anyone inside will hear it, loud.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.8:
§lInside§r

Build as you would anywhere. A new globe is empty: bring what you'll build with. Nothing inside is made from nothing, and nothing is lost.

To leave, right-click the glass wall with an empty hand.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.9:
§lSeasons§r

Shake a snow globe and the year turns: winter, spring, summer, autumn.

Shaken into winter, real snow settles on everything inside. Shaken into spring, it melts away.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.10:
§lSkies§r

Every globe has a sky of its own: blue over the snow, an endless sunset over the dunes, night in the star globe, storm grey, deep water blue in the aquarium, and red in the nether jar.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.11:
§lCompany§r

Animals on a lead come in with you.

Fish go in from their bucket, into the globe's water (there must be some). A water bucket catches one back out.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.12:
§lOn display§r

A §8collector's shelf§r holds two globes and keeps up with what's built in them: two sticks over three slabs.

A §8turntable§r spins whatever globe stands on it: a slab, gold and redstone, on dark oak.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.13:
§lBigger worlds§r

A Create schematic, right-clicked onto an empty globe, is built inside it, and the globe grows to fit. In survival, you pay for every block.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.14:
§lGlobes in globes§r

A globe can stand inside another, and you can go in deeper still. Leaving takes you out one glass at a time.
worldsinglass.creatures.no_water: There's no water in this globe for them to swim in.
worldsinglass.tooltip.scene: A little world is waiting inside
worldsinglass.handbook.page.15:
§lTwins§r

A globe with a world in it, an empty globe of the same kind and an ender pearl, crafted together, make a §8twin§r. You get both back: two globes, one world.

Keep one at home and give the other away. Step in through either.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.16:
§lNames, and finding globes§r

Use a name tag on a globe, or name it in an anvil, and its name goes on a brass plate on the base. An axe scrapes it off again.

Wandering traders sometimes sell a globe with a little world already waiting in it; old chests hide a few, too.
worldsinglass.handbook.page.17:
Keep them out of the sun, and dust them now and then.

And if you ever hear a knock from inside one of yours, it's only polite to knock back.

§o- O.
